newsitem.title: USA: Cigna gets clearance on HealthSource merger.
newsitem.headline: Cigna gets clearance on HealthSource merger.

text.p: Cigna Corp said Thursday it received federal antitrust clearance to proceed with its previously announced tender offer, through a unit, to acquire Healthsource Inc in a deal valued at $1.65 billion.

Under the tender offer, CHC Acquisition Corp would pay shareholders of the Hookset, N.H., company $21.75 per share. The offer, originally set to expire April 2, had been extended to Wednesday, April 30.

As the waiting period for the deal required under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976 expired at midnight on Wednesday, April 16, it said a condition to consummation of the offer has been satisfied.
It said the offer remains subject to state regulatory approvals.
It added that, according to IBJ Schroder Bank & Trust Co, the depositary for the offer, as of April 16, some 33.8 million shares of HealthSource had been validly tendered.
Cigna, with 1996 assets of $99 billion and revenues of $19 billion, is a leading provider of health care, insurance and related financial services throughout the United States and internationally.
